c.tagline: West Sumatra's coastal capital of rendang, sunsets, and surf-island gateways.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird operates metered taxis; insist on the meter, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front car and motorbike pricing, which is the norm for most visitors.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service. Padang lies on a seismic coast, so note tsunami evacuation routes and shelters.

avoid.reason: Watch bags in Pasar Raya market and on angkot minibuses, and note city beaches have strong currents and are best left before dark.

hood_desc: The downtown core around the Pasar Raya market, banks and offices, a short walk from the beach; the most central and convenient base for first-time visitors.
The Dutch-and-Chinese colonial old city along the Batang Arau river near Muaro harbour, with heritage warehouses, Chinatown, the Siti Nurbaya bridge and park; best for history and atmosphere.
The Taplau seafront strip (Pantai Padang/Purus), lined with beachfront hotels, sunset food stalls and the city's evening promenade; a breezy, sea-facing base.
A quieter residential and university district (Andalas/State University campuses) near the striking Grand Mosque of West Sumatra; calm and local, good for a slower pace.
The modern hotel-and-business avenue of Jalan Khatib Sulaiman, home to newer chain hotels, malls and government offices; a practical, contemporary base away from the old center.
lodging: Capital O 90643 Suri Guest House Syariah
Whiz Prime Hotel Khatib Sulaiman Padang

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; the tap supply is not potable.

transit.hours: Trans Padang BRT buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM along the Lubuk Buaya-Pasar Raya corridor; angkot run through the day, with Gojek/Grab filling late-night gaps.
transit.note: Padang has no rail metro; the backbone is the Trans Padang bus rapid transit (a single ~18 km corridor from Lubuk Buaya to Pasar Raya) alongside the colorful local angkot minibuses, plus Gojek/Grab and a commuter train (Sibinuang) running north to Pariaman.
transit.pay: Trans Padang and angkot fares are paid in cash to the conductor or driver (a few thousand rupiah); ride-hailing apps and QRIS e-wallets cover app-based trips. There is no integrated transit card.

sys.n: KA Sibinuang / Minangkabau Airport Rail Link

bus: Intercity buses from regional terminals to Bukittinggi, Pekanbaru and across Sumatra

car.idp: Recommended (International Driving Permit required alongside home license)

ferry: Teluk Bayur port and Muaro harbour: passenger ferries and fast boats to the Mentawai Islands (Siberut, Sipora, Pagai) for surfing, plus routes to Sibolga/Nias

transit.m: Minangkabau Airport Rail Link train to Padang (Simpang Haru) station (~30 min)
Damri airport bus to city center (~45 min)
Airport taxi to central Padang (30-45 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a service charge is often included at larger restaurants and hotels, and rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Masjid Raya Sumatera Barat (Grand Mosque of West Sumatra)
A breathtaking modern mosque whose sweeping roof mimics both the Minangkabau buffalo-horn silhouette and the cloth that carried the Black Stone of Mecca.
Kota Tua Padang (Old Town)
A weathered riverside quarter of Dutch trading houses, Chinese shophouses and vintage bridges along the Batang Arau, echoing Padang's colonial port heyday.
Jembatan Siti Nurbaya (Siti Nurbaya Bridge)
A 600-meter bridge over the Batang Arau named for Padang's tragic literary heroine, beloved at dusk for grilled corn stalls and harbor views.
Gunung Padang (Padang Hill)
The legendary headland above the river mouth, laced with trails past Japanese wartime bunkers to Siti Nurbaya's supposed grave and sweeping ocean panoramas.
Pantai Air Manis & Malin Kundang Stone
A broad brown-sand beach famed for the kneeling stone of Malin Kundang, the son cursed to rock for betraying his mother in Minangkabau legend.
Museum Adityawarman
West Sumatra's provincial museum, set in a soaring buffalo-horned Rumah Gadang, displaying Minangkabau wedding regalia, textiles and ceremonial heirlooms amid manicured gardens.
Pantai Padang (Taplau)
The city's lively seafront esplanade, where families gather for satay and coconuts as fiery Indian Ocean sunsets silhouette the fishing boats.
See Hin Kiong Temple
Padang's oldest Chinese temple, a red-and-gold 19th-century Buddhist landmark in the compact Chinatown, rebuilt with devotion after repeated earthquakes.
Pasumpahan Island
A tiny jewel of white sand and clear snorkeling water off Padang's coast, reached by short boat hop from Bungus Bay.
Lembah Anai Waterfall
A 35-meter roadside cascade plunging from rainforest cliffs beside the historic Padang-Bukittinggi road, the classic photo stop on any day trip inland.

train.note: No international trains. West Sumatra has a short surviving network: the Minangkabau Ekspres airport train links Padang with Minangkabau International Airport in about 30 minutes, and a heritage line climbs toward Padang Panjang and Sawahlunto. There is no through service to the rest of Sumatra, so intercity travel is by road.

bus.note: No international coaches. Terminal Bingkuang and the travel-minibus offices around town run north to Bukittinggi (about 2-3 hours), south toward Bengkulu and the long haul to Medan (around 20 hours) and Jakarta via the Bakauheni ferry. ANS and NPM are the established operators; book through redBus Indonesia (https://www.redbus.id/).

intl.to: Mentawai Islands - Siberut, Sipora & the Pagais (Indonesia) - overnight, ~10-12 hr
intl.op: ASDP and Mentawai Fast — tickets at Bungus and Muaro harbours

ferry.note: No international sailings. The Mentawai boats are the reason most travellers use this port - the islands are a world surfing destination with no other access. Slow overnight ferries leave from Bungus, about 20 km south of Padang, a few days a week, with faster boats from Muaro when running. Schedules change with the season and the swell, so confirm locally and allow spare days.

half.name: Bukittinggi
half.blurb: Cool Minangkabau highland town ~2 hrs northeast with the Jam Gadang clock tower, Sianok Canyon and WWII Japanese caves.

half.name: Anai Valley & Padang Panjang
half.blurb: Scenic drive past the Anai Valley waterfall to Minangkabau cultural sites and cool mountain air.

half.name: Air Manis Beach
half.blurb: The cursed-son Malin Kundang legend on a broad low-tide beach just south of the city.

full.name: Mentawai Islands
full.blurb: World-class surf breaks and Mentawai tribal culture, reached by ferry or fast boat from Teluk Bayur (overnight+).

full.name: Harau Valley
full.blurb: Dramatic rice-paddy valley walled by sheer granite cliffs and waterfalls near Payakumbuh, ~3 hrs.
